acceptance: The owner's recorded choice (A, B or C) is quoted at the top of the PR description's rationale; the implementation matches only that choice.

Outcome A: a unit test that records event order shows no database query touching ORDERS or LINEITEM between the start of the first refresh interval and any check, and no refresh-data query before the RF timer starts; the same test fails against the base commit.

Outcome A: injecting a duplicate key into the RF1 update set makes the post-commit RF1 check fail the phase with an error that names the update set and says the database needs a reload; injecting a short RF2 delete count fails RF2 likewise.
Outcome B or C: the corresponding test (flag in result metadata, or checks measured inside the interval) fails against the base commit and passes after.
uv run -- pytest tests/unit/core/tpch/test_tpch_refresh.py tests/unit/core/throughput passes, with the test that pinned the old placement replaced rather than duplicated.
Smoke: a DuckDB TPC-H SF0.01 run with refresh functions enabled completes; result evidence shows RF1 and RF2 SUCCESS and the check outcomes recorded.
docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md rows for RF1, RF2 and the refresh stream state the new placement; changelog fragment notes that refresh timings from earlier versions used the old placement.
context: Origin: 2026-11-03 root-cause analysis of TPC-H RF1 timing (5 whys) and its adversarial review. Spec clauses cited here were read from the published PDFs at the links on 2026-11-03; re-read them rather than trusting this text.
description:
Implement the option the owner recorded in tpch-refresh-precheck-timing-decision-20261103. Do not start until that item is done and its context quotes the owner's choice. perf-tpch-rf1-bulk-load-20261031 is a prerequisite only because both change the same refresh call sites in power_test.py, throughput_test.py and refresh.py; landing them in sequence avoids conflicting edits.

Scope by outcome (implement only the recorded one):
A (checks after the timer): remove check_rf1_preconditions and check_rf2_preconditions from before the RF timer in TPCHPowerTest._execute_refresh_function and the throughput refresh stream. RF1: after commit, verify the inserted keys exist exactly once and that the row counts match the update set. RF2: use the delete counts the driver reports plus the existing check_rf2_applied. A failing check still fails the phase and withholds Power@Size/Throughput@Size evidence as today. Rewrite the test pinned to the old behaviour (test_throughput_runs_all_safety_checks_outside_the_refresh_measurement) to pin the new behaviour; do not keep both.
B (keep, document): add the documented deviation and a result-metadata flag that makes official QphH export ineligible; no timing change.
C (checks inside the timer): move them inside and record the measured cost in the changelog.

Guardrails: Guardrails for all code work: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create); never edit the primary clone. No explanatory comments or docstrings in source (make comment-policy-check). Durations use benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()/elapsed_seconds(). Add a changelog.d/ fragment. Cited line numbers are orientation only: re-read the named symbols, docs and spec clauses before editing and treat a mismatch as a reason to stop and update this item. No live-cloud runs without owner approval; heavy runs only through make heavy-run or a lock-taking entry point. Green focused tests are not release certification. Any check removed from before the timer must exist after it; a safety check is never deleted. A failed refresh leaves the database mutated: the error text must say the database needs a reload and name the update set. Results produced under the old placement must be distinguishable from new ones (changelog states the change; if result metadata already carries a timing-method field, use it).
